standard_prerequisites.name: The affine etale neighbourhood with projective global sections, the purity criterion and constructibility of the relative assassin
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, labels lemma-finite-presentation-flat-along-fibre (proof line 6701), lemma-affine-locally-projective-pure (proof line 6714), lemma-criterion (proof line 6716) and lemma-universally-separating (proof line 6735); More on Morphisms, label more-morphisms-lemma-relative-assassin-constructible (proof line 6725); Morphisms, label morphisms-lemma-constructible-containing-open (proof line 6728); Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-flattening-module-map (proof line 6742)
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the affine etale neighbourhood and the etale g with projective global sections, places the relative associated points inside the image of g so that they can be removed after shrinking, reduces injectivity to the pulled back map, and finally identifies the representing ideal with the one constructed by the module map flatterling lemma.

core_obligations: Reduce to a local statement for the etale topology: F is universally pure over S, and by the sheaf property of F_iso together with descent of closed immersions and of descent data the question is local for the etale topology on S, so it suffices to prove the theorem after passing to an etale neighbourhood of an arbitrary point s (proof lines 6686-6697).

Remove the relative associated points: using the flat along the fibre lemma and an elementary etale neighbourhood one may assume an affine diagram with X' and S affine, g etale, X_s inside g(X') and the global sections of g^*F projective over the ring of S; by purity of the pulled back module and the purity criterion the open g(X') contains the relative associated points over the localisation of S at s, so the constructible set of points of S where the associated points of the fibre lie in g(X') contains that localisation, hence an open neighbourhood of s, and after shrinking S one may assume all relative associated points lie in g(X') (proof lines 6699-6731).

Reduce to the affine projective case: since u is surjective, F_iso equals F_inj, and the universality lemma shows injectivity of u is equivalent to injectivity of the pulled back map, and stays so after base change; this reduces to the case where X -> S is a morphism of affine schemes and the global sections of F are projective over the ring of S, which is exactly the case settled by the module map flatterling lemma (proof lines 6733-6742).

Finite presentation of the representing object: if G is of finite presentation, combine part (4) of the functor lemma with the remark that a limit preserving representable functor is represented by a scheme of finite presentation (proof lines 6744-6749).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an etale neighbourhood of an arbitrary point using the sheaf and descent properties (proof lines 6686-6697).
Use purity to place the relative associated points inside the image of the etale morphism and shrink the base accordingly (proof lines 6699-6731).
Reduce injectivity to an affine projective module statement and apply the module map flatterling lemma (proof lines 6733-6742).
Derive finite presentation of the representing closed subscheme from the limit preserving property (proof lines 6744-6749).
difficulty_reason: The theorem represents the functor of points where a surjection of modules becomes an isomorphism by a closed immersion Z -> S, in the finite presentation and flat and pure case, and makes Z of finite presentation when the target module is (statement lines 6670-6684, tag 05PF). The counted proof is a genuine reduction chain: it moves to the etale topology using the sheaf property and descent of closed immersions, builds an affine etale neighbourhood on which the global sections are projective, uses purity and the purity criterion to show that the relative associated points lie in the image of the etale morphism after shrinking the base, and then reduces injectivity of the pulled back map to a statement about projective modules over an affine base that the module map flatterling lemma settles. The associated prime shrinking step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
